name: What should I compare when I get multiple quotes for my living room remodel?

mainEntity.name: What should I compare when I get multiple quotes for my living room remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A good remodel proposal should define the existing conditions, design scope, materials, labor, allowances, exclusions, schedule assumptions, permits, inspections, cleanup, warranty terms, and change-order process. Comparing only the bottom-line price can hide major differences in what each contractor has included.

**Context:** Elite Remodeling & Design combines design, material selections, construction coordination, and inspections within its described process. That makes it especially useful to ask where design decisions end and construction responsibilities begin.

**Key factors:**
- Whether plans, 3D visualization, selections, and revisions are included.
- Who obtains permits and coordinates inspections.
- Allowances for flooring, lighting, built-ins, fireplace work, and finish materials.
- Protection, demolition, disposal, punch-list, and final cleanup.

**Practical guidance:** Give each contractor the same written scope and ask for exclusions in writing. Request clarification for concealed damage, owner-supplied materials, substitutions, schedule changes, and work outside the living room.

Elite Remodeling & Design can help turn a broad living room idea into a defined design-build scope for comparison.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare scope, plans, design services, material allowances, labor, permits, inspections, demolition, protection, cleanup, schedule assumptions, warranty terms, and change-order rules—not just the total price. Give every contractor the same written project description and require exclusions and concealed-condition handling in writing.
